Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.

During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.

Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly said he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.

Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House said Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.

Even after all this, Huang reportedly said he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

Early screenings of David Fincher’s latest film are raising questions about whether the director used generative AI.

Though David Fincher ’s fans had been eagerly anticipating The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, early screenings of the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel starring Brad Pitt have raised questions about whether generative AI was used in the film. People have claimed that the movie is chock-full of uncanny, inconsistent visuals that make it feel more like slop than the sort of polished film you’d expect from the director of sleek productions like Fight Club and The Social Network.

Following a number of Cliff Booth critics screenings that took place last week ahead of the film’s premiere on November 25th, moviegoers rushed to social media to lament what they saw. One of the most vocal reactions came from YouTuber / director Patrick Tomasso, who said on X that he walked out of his screening feeling “completely gutted” and that the film featured “some of the most blatant and egregious AI use” he has ever seen from a major studio. Tomasso also insisted you can see AI-generated footage in Cliff Booth ’s trailers that have been posted online, and he was confident that Fincher’s latest film is filled with “slop as you know and loathe it. The shit you can pump out of Higgsfield.”

Others echoed Tomasso’s sentiments, writing that “the amount of AI in the CLIFF BOOTH movie is astounding to an absurd degree” and vowing to “never watch another Fincher, Pitt or Tarintino [ sic ] movie again.” Yet some critics enjoyed the film and suggested that the bad AI people thought they were seeing might have actually just been bad CGI. Netflix has neither confirmed nor denied whether AI was used in any capacity to make the film, but Netflix’s heavy involvement in the film’s production and the company’s recent investments in generative AI technology left many suspicious.

It did not help that David Fincher, in a recent interview with the Los Angeles Times, responded to questions about his thoughts on AI with “I’m not a Luddite, so I don’t fear the unknown.” Fincher also reasoned that the anti-AI crowd is advocating for artists to stop iterating on their creative processes: “Is everyone satisfied that we have figured this art form out enough that what we really need to do is go back to celluloid? How long have people painted? 40,000 years? We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.’ Well, it exists. Should we not use it?” The spiel made it sound like he might be jumping on the AI bandwagon.

Set about a decade after Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, Cliff Booth picks up in 1977 at a time when Booth (Pitt) has left his life as a stuntman behind to become a fixer who quietly deals with scandalous problems for Hollywood elites. Cliff still works a number of side gigs as a projectionist and bartender. But the movie is primarily focused on his budding romance with critic-turned-talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) and his working relationship with Charlie Peters (Scott Caan), a TV actor who needs Booth’s services to keep his wife (Carla Gugino) from being murdered.

items.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
items.summary: The British cyber agency says that "building strong foundations has never mattered more" as AI hacking tools rely on exploiting simple security flaws.
full_paragraphs: The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says it has seen a “marked rise” in AI-driven cyberattacks in recent months, as hackers increasingly rely on autonomous hacking tools to identify and exploit simple weaknesses to break into systems and networks.

The U.K. National Cybersecurity Center (NCSC) said it has seen several cyber incidents since September involving autonomous hacking tools, such as penetration testing tools used by defenders to stress-test their cybersecurity defenses. These incidents have caused intrusions at organizations and resulted in downtime, the unit said in a blog post.
The NCSC says that while none of the vulnerabilities being exploited are new, the speed at which these AI tools are able to carry out simple hacks has changed.

The rise in AI-related cyberattacks coincides with the broader release earlier this year of open source autonomous penetration testing tools like Artex and Cairn, among others, which anyone can download and use at no cost. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation recently warned that malicious hackers are using AI penetration testing tools to carry out cyberattacks at unprecedented speeds.
While cyberattacks and intrusions are on the rise, the message from London is that many of these attacks are preventable with basic cybersecurity defenses and best practices.

“Notably, the issues being exploited currently are not novel memory corruption vulnerabilities (or even known but unpatched vulnerabilities), but unmitigated weaknesses that are often the result of years of technical debt that organisations have accumulated,” the NCSC wrote.

The unit said that agentic hacking tools often look for exposed or internet-facing systems, then quickly run through lists of weak or easy-to-guess passwords or abuse API endpoints often used by developers to access data.
The NCSC said that AI “does not make established cyber security controls obsolete,” but rather that “building strong foundations has never mattered more.”

O Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança do Reino Unido (NCSC) disse ter visto vários incidentes cibernéticos desde setembro envolvendo ferramentas de hacking autônomas, como ferramentas de teste de penetração usadas pelos defensores para testar a resistência de suas defesas de segurança cibernética. Esses incidentes causaram intrusões nas organizações e resultaram em tempo de inatividade, disse a unidade em um blog.
O NCSC afirma que, embora nenhuma das vulnerabilidades exploradas seja nova, a velocidade com que essas ferramentas de IA são capazes de realizar hacks simples mudou.

O aumento dos ataques cibernéticos relacionados com a IA coincide com o lançamento mais amplo, no início deste ano, de ferramentas autónomas de testes de penetração de código aberto, como Artex e Cairn, entre outras, que qualquer pessoa pode descarregar e utilizar gratuitamente. O Federal Bureau of Investigation dos EUA alertou recentemente que hackers mal-intencionados estão usando ferramentas de testes de penetração de IA para realizar ataques cibernéticos em velocidades sem precedentes.

Embora os ataques cibernéticos e as intrusões estejam a aumentar, a mensagem de Londres é que muitos destes ataques podem ser evitados com defesas básicas de segurança cibernética e melhores práticas.

“Notavelmente, os problemas explorados atualmente não são novas vulnerabilidades de corrupção de memória (ou mesmo vulnerabilidades conhecidas, mas não corrigidas), mas fraquezas absolutas que muitas vezes são o resultado de anos de dívida técnica que as organizações acumularam”, escreveu o NCSC.

A unidade disse que as ferramentas de hackers geralmente procuram sistemas expostos ou voltados para a Internet e, em seguida, executam rapidamente listas de senhas fracas ou fáceis de adivinhar ou abusam de endpoints de API frequentemente usados ​​​​por desenvolvedores para acessar dados.
O NCSC disse que a IA “não torna obsoletos os controles de segurança cibernética estabelecidos”, mas sim que “construir bases sólidas nunca foi tão importante”.

Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.

The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated. In a post on X, Andersen says Tidal needed to take a more “drastic” measure, as AI music made up 43 percent of the tracks distributed to the platform in the last 90 days. “We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all,” Andersen adds.

Bandcamp similarly banned AI music earlier this year, while other music streaming platforms attempt to address a flood of AI songs by applying new labels or removing them from user algorithms. Spotify recently announced that it removed 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from recommendations over the past year, and also launched new “AI persona” badges for artists that use an AI identity. YouTube has rolled out AI music labels as well, while Apple Music is planning to launch AI labels this year. Meanwhile, Deezer is giving users the option to filter out AI music.

“Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale: It diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans,” Tidal says in a separate post on X.

The platform is also going to ban music distributors from submitting AI songs, using the AI detection tool Ircam Amplify and metadata checks to reject submissions generated solely with AI. Tidal notes that it won’t ban songs made with the assistance of AI tools, as long as AI doesn’t make up the “sole output.”

full_paragraphs: Instagram users can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the company announced on Tuesday. The social media network says users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs.

The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content.
Users can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.
Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app.
Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore.

Meta also announced that users can now do more with the posts and reels they’ve bookmarked on Instagram. For example, they can ask Muse to organize their saved content into custom folders, known as Collections. They could also ask Muse to turn a recipe video into a grocery list, turn the travel content from their favorite travel creators into an itinerary for an upcoming trip, or have Muse send them outfit ideas based on fashion reels they’ve collected.
Starting Tuesday, when users save a post on Instagram, they will see a prompt for Muse to organize it for them. This feature is launching in the U.S. and Canada.

Meta says that users remain in control of their Muse experience on Instagram. Nothing is shared, published, or sent without their approval, and they can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions at any time.

full_paragraphs: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.

Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.
Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services, said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.
Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, said on X.

A few months ago, @Tidal tagged and demonetized all wholly AI-generated tracks to protect the authenticity of real artists. But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done…
The company said that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.

full_paragraphs: Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.
Influencers are chasing viral success with the saga — and tech stack — of Nvidia’s CEO.
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza. In a video with nearly 6 million views on Instagram, the former CEO of Nvidia is dancing in a crowded club, champagne glass in hand, still wearing his signature black leather jacket. Suddenly, from behind him, Alice Huang — the Chinese technology executive and suspected spy he had an affair with, sparking congressional investigations and his resignation from the chipmaking company he cofounded — appears. She puts her hand on his shoulder and he wraps his arm around her waist as they begin dancing together. The video’s caption reads “Honey Trap Final Boss. #inthemoodforlove.”

Of course, it’s AI-generated. This Instagram Reel is one of hundreds of AI deepfakes featuring Huang, his wife Lori, Alice, and sometimes Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, Kimberly Powell (the second of three reported affair partners ). In this case, Huang is being swapped into an existing meme called “ Ibiza Final Boss.” The original video featured a British construction worker with a bowl cut dancing in exactly the same way, minus a woman sidling up to him. Other viral AI hits include Huang in a scene from The Office, Huang in the music video for George Michael’s “Careless Whisper,” and Huang as the former Astronomer CEO who got caught in an affair with one of his employees by the jumbotron at a Coldplay concert last summer. Even the rapper 50 Cent posted an AI edit of his “P.I.M.P.” music video, now featuring Huang with some flashy silver accessories.

Unlike deepfake pornography or election disinformation, these AI videos aren’t necessarily intended to harm or mislead people. They’re memes making fun of Huang’s cheating scandal and its global implications, created with AI technology that in many cases relies heavily on Nvidia’s tech stack: video diffusion models running on the Nvidia GPUs that power much of the modern generative AI industry. “It’s ironic that without Nvidia generating millions of these AI memes... would not be possible,” reads one of the top comments on the Ibiza deepfake. “In some sense, Jensen is making Nvidia richer by his own scandal.” The comment was punctuated by multiple cry-laughing emoji.

As it turns out, Huang may benefit, too. On Monday, the Nvidia board announced he was reinstated as president, CEO, and board director following “a series of discussions and meetings” and “input from senior levels of the United States government.” Nvidia’s stock has since surged, and new AI Huang memes cast him in a victorious light. One variation swaps him into a scene from The Wolf of Wall Street, announcing “I’m not leaving” to a crowd of cheering men that has been edited to include AI versions of Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and Mark Zuckerberg.

While the saga continues, many social media users are finding the humor in these Huang deepfakes, and their creators are churning out variations to meet the sudden demand. The Instagram account behind the Ibiza one has made three Huang deepfakes so far, all remakes of the same scene. Another version features Powell dancing with him, and the third one shows a sea of young women in bikini tops and shorts surrounding Huang, who lifts his champagne up in celebration. Each has accrued millions of views.

items.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
items.summary: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.
full_paragraphs: The problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year.

“Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.”

It’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants, but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster.
That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market.

“Global capacity of natural gas is only about 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, where solar is already at well over a terawatt,” he said. “Probably the most important lesson that we’ve learned over the last 20 years of backing companies is that Wright’s Law is the thing you want to leverage — making the same thing over and over again.”

Both solar and most forms of long-duration energy storage are built on small, modular technologies that can be manufactured at massive scale. “This is about speed and scale and economics, and we can win across all those dimensions,” Porter said.

G2VP had an early window into AI data center development, having led Crusoe’s Series C. “We’ve had a front-row seat at what’s been happening at that company, how they’ve evolved, how the different waves of data centers have evolved,” Porter said.

The venture firm estimates that data center investment will top $4 trillion until the end of the decade. As the next wave takes shape, the firm sees two different paths for data centers: small, on-grid facilities with their own generating capacity, and larger data centers powered by solar and long-duration energy storage.

full_paragraphs: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers.

As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening. As few as half of enterprises believe their current networks can handle AI’s bandwidth and latency demands, according to a recent study.
This report explores how treating network modernization as an on-going strategy rather than a one-off project can help organizations adapt in the face of disruption and uncertainty.

AI may force companies to shift from a cloud-first approach to routing workloads. Training AI requires server-to-server data center architectures, while inference calls for low-latency connectivity close to users. Enterprises may need to fundamentally reconsider their network architecture to meet these requirements.

AI inference is pushing infrastructure back on premises. Inference typically requires real-time processing and is sensitive to latency, making hosting such capabilities on distant hyperscale clouds neither economical nor practical. Inconsistent latency can lead to AI model failures, driving up queue wait times, saturating GPUs loads, and causing bottlenecks in data flows. Large enterprises may need on-premises or near-premises inference, which reverses years of cloud-first consolidation and forces new approaches to data center architecture, connectivity, and physical infrastructure.

AI workloads are stressing physical network capacity in unexpected ways. The traffic increase from agentic AI, combined with inference moving on-premises, is exposing bandwidth bottlenecks in legacy underlay infrastructure.

Network modernization is an ongoing project that requires a holistic approach, allowing companies to adapt with ease. A combination of strong architectural governance, reusable design templates, and retained internal expertise supports organizations in adapting to disruptive events without rebuilding their infrastructure from scratch each time. Such events could include mergers and acquisitions, changing vendors, or technology upgrades.

NaaS and AI-driven observability can improve efficiency and reduce complexity in network operations. Network-as-a-service (NaaS) and AI-driven observability can offer companies benefits like faster, more flexible provisioning and lower costs.

full_paragraphs_pt: As redes empresariais estão sob forte pressão. À medida que as empresas se apressam em implementar a inteligência artificial, a tecnologia está rapidamente a tornar-se a maior fonte de procura na rede. Agora, a IA agente está aumentando a carga. As tarefas conduzidas por agentes de IA geram cerca de 450% mais tráfego de rede do que as mesmas tarefas realizadas por trabalhadores humanos.

À medida que a inferência de IA muda de nuvens de treinamento em hiperescala – os enormes data centers centralizados onde os modelos brutos de IA ingerem vastos conjuntos de dados e aprendem – para aplicativos em tempo real e sensíveis à latência, cresce a necessidade de infraestrutura local ou próxima. Como resultado, a lacuna entre as redes empresariais que estão prontas para apoiar a IA e aquelas que não estão está aumentando. Apenas metade das empresas acredita que as suas redes atuais podem lidar com as exigências de largura de banda e latência da IA, de acordo com um estudo recente.
Este relatório explora como tratar a modernização da rede como uma estratégia contínua, em vez de um projeto único, pode ajudar as organizações a se adaptarem diante de interrupções e incertezas.

A IA pode forçar as empresas a mudar de uma abordagem que prioriza a nuvem para rotear cargas de trabalho. A IA de treinamento requer arquiteturas de data center servidor a servidor, enquanto a inferência exige conectividade de baixa latência próxima aos usuários. As empresas podem precisar reconsiderar fundamentalmente a sua arquitetura de rede para atender a esses requisitos.

A inferência de IA está empurrando a infraestrutura de volta para o local. A inferência normalmente requer processamento em tempo real e é sensível à latência, tornando a hospedagem de tais recursos em nuvens distantes em hiperescala nem econômica nem prática. A latência inconsistente pode levar a falhas no modelo de IA, aumentando os tempos de espera nas filas, saturando cargas de GPUs e causando gargalos nos fluxos de dados. As grandes empresas podem precisar de inferência local ou próxima, o que reverte anos de consolidação da nuvem e força novas abordagens à arquitetura, conectividade e infraestrutura física do data center.

As cargas de trabalho de IA estão sobrecarregando a capacidade da rede física de maneiras inesperadas. O aumento do tráfego da IA ​​de agência, combinado com a movimentação de inferências no local, está expondo gargalos de largura de banda na infraestrutura subjacente herdada.

A modernização da rede é um projeto contínuo que requer uma abordagem holística, permitindo que as empresas se adaptem com facilidade. Uma combinação de forte governança arquitetônica, modelos de design reutilizáveis ​​e conhecimento interno retido apoia as organizações na adaptação a eventos disruptivos sem precisar reconstruir sua infraestrutura do zero a cada vez. Tais eventos podem incluir fusões e aquisições, mudanças de fornecedores ou atualizações tecnológicas.

A observabilidade orientada por NaaS e IA pode melhorar a eficiência e reduzir a complexidade nas operações de rede. A observabilidade baseada em rede como serviço (NaaS) e IA pode oferecer às empresas benefícios como provisionamento mais rápido e flexível e custos mais baixos.

items.title: Production AI Playbook: Audit & trace for AI agents
items.summary: Reconstruct an AI decision, and retain the records needed to explain it later. Five hands-on n8n exercises: reading saved executions, tagging decisions for search, tracing tool calls with OpenTelemetry, and proving which workflow version ran.
full_paragraphs: This post is part of a series that explores proven strategies and practical examples for building reliable AI systems. If you are new to n8n, start with the introduction.

Your refund agent has been live for a month. It reads each customer message, looks up the order, and approves small refunds on its own. Then the finance team flags a $49.99 refund that should never have gone out and asks why the agent approved it. You open the workflow to find out, but the prompt has been edited twice since then, the order record has changed, and nobody recorded which run made that decision. The reality is that the workflow in front of you today cannot explain a decision it made last month.

This is what's called the audit gap. Every team that lets an AI workflow act on its own runs into it once real requests start coming in. A decision you cannot reconstruct is a decision you will end up defending from memory. An audit trail closes the gap by keeping the evidence behind each decision, including the original inputs, the workflow version, and any human approval. Tracing connects the steps of a run across workflows and services and records their timing and status. Together, they give you the records to answer the finance team's question.
The exercises below build up that record in n8n Cloud, starting with one saved execution, then adding decision tags and traces to follow tool calls and a human approval.

When you question a decision, start with the saved execution. It is n8n's record of a single run, and it shows what each node received and returned. In a refund workflow, that means you can see what the order lookup returned and what the agent told the customer. Comparing the two can reveal a reply the data does not support, even when the run reports success.

Apply this check to a support agent that generates refund replies from a simulated order lookup. Compare a complete record with two unusable records, then enable validation to route the missing-data cases to human review.

2. In the workflow’s three-dot menu, select Settings, set Save manual executions to Save, then click Save. Use this setting for each exercise workflow.
items.title_pt: Manual de produção de IA: auditoria e rastreamento para agentes de IA
items.summary_pt: Reconstrua uma decisão de IA e guarde os registros necessários para explicá-la posteriormente. Cinco exercícios práticos n8n: leitura de execuções salvas, marcação de decisões para pesquisa, rastreamento de chamadas de ferramentas com OpenTelemetry e comprovação de qual versão do fluxo de trabalho foi executada.
full_paragraphs_pt: Esta postagem faz parte de uma série que explora estratégias comprovadas e exemplos práticos para a construção de sistemas de IA confiáveis. Se você é novo no n8n, comece com a introdução.

Seu agente de reembolso está ativo há um mês. Ele lê a mensagem de cada cliente, consulta o pedido e aprova pequenos reembolsos por conta própria. Em seguida, a equipe financeira sinaliza um reembolso de US$ 49,99 que nunca deveria ter sido emitido e pergunta por que o agente o aprovou. Você abre o fluxo de trabalho para descobrir, mas o prompt foi editado duas vezes desde então, o registro do pedido foi alterado e ninguém registrou qual execução tomou essa decisão. A realidade é que o fluxo de trabalho que você tem hoje não consegue explicar uma decisão tomada no mês passado.

Isto é o que chamamos de lacuna de auditoria. Cada equipe que permite que um fluxo de trabalho de IA atue por conta própria se depara com ele assim que solicitações reais começam a chegar. Uma decisão que você não pode reconstruir é uma decisão que você acabará defendendo de memória. Uma trilha de auditoria preenche a lacuna, mantendo as evidências por trás de cada decisão, incluindo as informações originais, a versão do fluxo de trabalho e qualquer aprovação humana. O rastreamento conecta as etapas de uma execução entre fluxos de trabalho e serviços e registra seu tempo e status. Juntos, eles fornecem os registros para responder à pergunta da equipe financeira.

Os exercícios abaixo constroem esse registro no n8n Cloud, começando com uma execução salva e, em seguida, adicionando tags de decisão e rastreamentos para seguir as chamadas de ferramenta e uma aprovação humana.

Ao questionar uma decisão, comece com a execução salva. É o registro de uma única execução do n8n e mostra o que cada nó recebeu e retornou. Em um fluxo de trabalho de reembolso, isso significa que você pode ver o que a pesquisa do pedido retornou e o que o agente disse ao cliente. A comparação dos dois pode revelar uma resposta que os dados não suportam, mesmo quando a execução reporta sucesso.

Aplique esta verificação a um agente de suporte que gera respostas de reembolso a partir de uma consulta de pedido simulado. Compare um registro completo com dois registros inutilizáveis ​​e ative a validação para encaminhar os casos de dados ausentes para revisão humana.

2. No menu de três pontos do fluxo de trabalho, selecione Configurações, defina Salvar execuções manuais como Salvar e clique em Salvar. Use this setting for each exercise workflow.

full_paragraphs: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.

The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.

full_paragraphs: Two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to look for signs of planets in public telescope data. Now they’ve given professional astronomers a few places to look more closely.

Astronomers have confirmed more than 6,400 planets beyond our solar system ⁠ (opens in a new window) since the first ones were announced in 1992 ⁠ (opens in a new window). A worldwide community of amateur astronomers has long been part of that search. Some comb through public telescope data for small, repeated dips in a star’s brightness that could signal an orbiting planet. Others use their own telescopes to watch for the next dip and share what they see with researchers.
*Data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive’s Planetary Systems Composite Parameters table ⁠ (opens in a new window). 2026 data are year to date through November 24, 2026.

Astronomers have used AI in this search for years. In 2017, researchers trained a neural network on 15,000 signals from NASA’s Kepler Space Telescope ⁠ (opens in a new window) that astronomers had already examined. From those examples, the model learned to recognize which patterns in starlight were most likely to come from a planet. When the researchers used it to examine weaker signals, one led them to an eighth planet orbiting a star called Kepler-90 ⁠ (opens in a new window).

Now, tools like Astra are helping amateur astronomers design and run searches of their own, often on data that has already yielded the more obvious exoplanet signals. Kevin Bond, an engineer at OpenAI, came to astronomy through his love of photographing the night sky. He used Codex to search observations of about 100,000 stars from the Kepler telescope, a planet-hunting mission that ran from 2009 to 2018. Ethan Byrd, founder of the email infrastructure start-up Primitive, has always loved astronomy. Working independently of Bond, he tried several AI models before choosing Astra to help him analyze telescope data from about 19 million stars.

Both searches identified potential exoplanets. Bond and Byrd have now turned to astronomers for an independent assessment of their results. Bond contacted an astronomer at the SETI Institute, who ran an independent search and found two of the same signals in the Kepler data. Byrd sent one of his strongest candidates to researchers working on NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. It’s in line for further analysis, and two more candidates are awaiting submission.

One of the most common ways to find an exoplanet is to watch the star it orbits. When a planet passes in front of its star from our point of view on Earth, it blocks a tiny amount of starlight. Astronomers call that crossing a transit. On a graph of the star’s brightness over time, known as a light curve, a transit shows up as a dip. If the dip keeps coming back at regular intervals, astronomers know when to watch for it again.

Searching for that pattern across thousands of stars is partly a coding problem. Astronomers have published methods for picking out faint, recurring dips in years of measurements. Bond used Codex to compare those methods, combine them in a search program, and test whether changes to the code improved the search. One AI agent scanned the light curves for promising signals. Another ran more detailed checks on the candidates the first one flagged.

Agora eles deram aos astrônomos profissionais alguns lugares para observar mais de perto. full_paragraphs_pt: Dois astrônomos amadores usaram o Codex e o Astra para procurar sinais de planetas em dados de telescópios públicos. Agora eles deram aos astrônomos profissionais alguns lugares para observar mais de perto.

Os astrônomos confirmaram mais de 6.400 planetas além do nosso sistema solar ⁠ (abre em uma nova janela) desde que os primeiros foram anunciados em 1992 ⁠ (abre em uma nova janela). Uma comunidade mundial de astrônomos amadores faz parte dessa busca há muito tempo. Alguns vasculham dados de telescópios públicos em busca de pequenas e repetidas quedas no brilho de uma estrela que possam sinalizar um planeta em órbita. Outros usam seus próprios telescópios para observar o próximo mergulho e compartilhar o que veem com os pesquisadores.
*Dados da tabela de parâmetros compostos de sistemas planetários do NASA Exoplanet Archive ⁠ (abre em uma nova janela). Os dados de 2026 são acumulados no ano até 24 de novembro de 2026.

Os astrônomos usam IA nesta busca há anos. Em 2017, os pesquisadores treinaram uma rede neural em 15.000 sinais do Telescópio Espacial Kepler da NASA ⁠ (abre em uma nova janela) que os astrônomos já haviam examinado. A partir desses exemplos, o modelo aprendeu a reconhecer quais padrões na luz das estrelas tinham maior probabilidade de vir de um planeta. Quando os pesquisadores o usaram para examinar sinais mais fracos, um deles os levou a um oitavo planeta orbitando uma estrela chamada Kepler-90 ⁠ (abre em uma nova janela).

Agora, ferramentas como o Astra estão a ajudar os astrónomos amadores a conceber e realizar pesquisas próprias, muitas vezes em dados que já produziram os sinais mais óbvios de exoplanetas. Kevin Bond, engenheiro da OpenAI, chegou à astronomia por causa de seu amor por fotografar o céu noturno. Ele usou o Codex para pesquisar observações de cerca de 100.000 estrelas do telescópio Kepler, uma missão de caça a planetas que ocorreu de 2009 a 2018. Ethan Byrd, fundador da startup de infraestrutura de e-mail Primitive, sempre amou astronomia. Trabalhando independentemente de Bond, ele experimentou vários modelos de IA antes de escolher o Astra para ajudá-lo a analisar dados telescópicos de cerca de 19 milhões de estrelas.

Ambas as pesquisas identificaram exoplanetas potenciais. Bond e Byrd recorreram agora aos astrónomos para uma avaliação independente dos seus resultados. Bond contatou um astrônomo do Instituto SETI, que realizou uma pesquisa independente e encontrou dois dos mesmos sinais nos dados do Kepler. Byrd enviou um de seus candidatos mais fortes para pesquisadores que trabalham na missão Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) da NASA. Está na fila para análise posterior e mais dois candidatos aguardam submissão.

Uma das maneiras mais comuns de encontrar um exoplaneta é observar a estrela que ele orbita. Quando um planeta passa na frente de sua estrela do nosso ponto de vista na Terra, ele bloqueia uma pequena quantidade de luz estelar. Os astrônomos chamam isso de trânsito. Num gráfico do brilho da estrela ao longo do tempo, conhecido como curva de luz, um trânsito aparece como uma queda. Se a queda continuar voltando em intervalos regulares, os astrônomos saberão quando observá-la novamente.

Procurar esse padrão em milhares de estrelas é, em parte, um problema de codificação. Os astrônomos publicaram métodos para detectar quedas fracas e recorrentes em anos de medições. Bond usou o Codex para comparar esses métodos, combiná-los em um programa de busca e testar se as alterações no código melhoraram a busca. Um agente de IA examinou as curvas de luz em busca de sinais promissores. Outro fez verificações mais detalhadas dos candidatos sinalizados pelo primeiro.

items.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
items.summary: Good morning, and welcome to our 3,697 new readers. The Jensen Huang saga already felt like a movie. On Monday, the scandal that had rocked the tech world for weeks hit its climax — the return. Jensen is back in the captain's seat at Nvidia, leather jacket and all, after President Donald Trump personally lobbied the board and its members voted unanimously to reinstate him. With it came $1T in market value, celebrations from the tech world, and fresh outrage on Capitol Hill.
full_paragraphs: Good morning, and welcome to our 3,697 new readers. The Jensen Huang saga already felt like a movie. On Monday, the scandal that had rocked the tech world for weeks hit its climax — the return.

Jensen is back in the captain's seat at Nvidia, leather jacket and all, after President Donald Trump personally lobbied the board and its members voted unanimously to reinstate him. With it came $1T in market value, celebrations from the tech world, and fresh outrage on Capitol Hill.

The Rundown: Nvidia's board just reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO only 11 days after he resigned over affairs with a direct report and a woman U.S. officials linked to Chinese intelligence, with President Trump saying he personally pushed for the return.
The unanimous vote came six days after chair Harvey Jones ruled out rehiring Huang, with the board saying “senior levels” of the U.S. government weighed in.
Huang said he takes the job back “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” thanking interim CEO Colette Kress, who stays on as CFO.
Trump told CNBC he'd been “speaking to the board directly and indirectly,” and posted that the government sees no reason to view Huang's return as a risk.
Nvidia shares jumped over 30% after the open and added over $1T in market value during trading, the single largest daily gain in the history of the stock market.
Huang still faces a House hearing in December, with Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries calling the move “indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible.”

full_paragraphs: Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.

As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.

One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.

We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as an LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.

Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.

This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.

In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.
items.title_pt: Investir no benefício público
items.summary_pt: Hoje, estamos comprometendo parte das ações da Anthropic com o Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic, uma nova entidade integral com uma estrutura que aumenta a participação à medida que a empresa cresce. full_paragraphs_pt: Hoje, estamos comprometendo parte das ações da Anthropic com o Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic, uma nova entidade integral com uma estrutura que aumenta a participação à medida que a empresa cresce. Sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, 5% das ações da Anthropic serão comprometidas hoje, com 2% adicionais adicionados a critério do conselho para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base definida.

Como uma empresa de utilidade pública, a maior parte do nosso trabalho na prossecução da nossa missão ocorre dentro da empresa: investigação relevante para a segurança e interpretabilidade da IA; pesquisa biomédica aplicada; descontos em Claude para organizações sem fins lucrativos e instituições científicas. Estas atividades têm uma componente de benefício público e um valor lucrativo, pelo que as alojamos diretamente na empresa.

O Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público terá maior flexibilidade e escala, permitindo-nos prosseguir a nossa missão de novas formas: por exemplo, poderemos explorar grandes doações para organizações sem fins lucrativos tradicionais ou distribuições diretas a populações específicas.

Um exemplo são os impactos no mercado de trabalho. A IA pode gerar um enorme valor económico, mas também pode causar instabilidade para muitos trabalhadores. A Anthropic já comprometeu 200 milhões de dólares para estudar e abordar esta questão, mas dado o ritmo do progresso da IA, poderão ser necessárias abordagens mais ousadas. O Fundo terá versatilidade para persegui-los.

Estamos estabelecendo o Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público como uma LLC – em vez de um 501(c)(3) ou outro formato – para oferecer ajuste entre diferentes formas de doação. Nenhum patrimônio da Antrópico detido pela LLC será usado para lobby ou doações políticas, nos EUA ou no exterior.

Pela forma como o Fundo está estruturado, quanto mais a Antrópica cresce, maior é a parcela da empresa que pode ser dedicada expressamente ao bem público. É prática comum que as empresas de tecnologia ofereçam prêmios crescentes de remuneração aos seus executivos. Em vez disso, estamos direcionando essa equidade para o benefício público.

Isto se baseia em compromissos que nossos cofundadores e funcionários já assumiram. Quando a Anthropic foi fundada, nossos cofundadores se comprometeram a doar 80% de suas participações acionárias e, desde a fundação, também operamos um programa de equiparação de doações de ações que permite aos funcionários prometer ações equivalentes à Anthropic. Aproximadamente metade dos nossos funcionários participa deste programa. Quando combinado com o anúncio de hoje, cerca de 20% das ações da Anthropic serão dedicadas ao bem público, além de qualquer porcentagem adicional que possa ser adicionada se a empresa atingir marcos de avaliação específicos.

Nos próximos meses, compartilharemos mais sobre a estrutura e governança do Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público, incluindo os marcos de avaliação que podem agregar à sua participação. Também informaremos sobre nosso progresso até o momento em relação à nossa missão em um próximo relatório de benefício público.

Ultralytics 8.4.217, released November 23, 2026, calibrates with entropy instead, and a newly built engine of the same model scores 0.4685.

The short answer to "why": max lets a handful of outlier activations set each tensor's INT8 range, so the values that matter lose resolution. entropy clips those outliers and keeps the shape of the distribution. This post explains the change, shows the measured results across tasks, covers the configurations where the gain did not carry over, and walks through exporting and checking an INT8 engine yourself.

The change began with issue #27334, opened by a community developer on November 23. They noticed that our TensorRT 11 export passed calibration_method="max" to NVIDIA ModelOpt, even though ModelOpt's own INT8 default is entropy, as its quantize API reference lists. Changing only that one argument on 8.4.216 gave higher accuracy on all three detection models they tried:

In a separate L4 run with four calibration images, they built each nano model's max engine twice from scratch and got the same mAP to four decimals. The Ultralytics team reproduced the result across all seven tasks the same day, and PR #27340 shipped it in 8.4.217 with the issue author credited as co-author.
INT8 quantization maps each tensor's values onto 256 levels. Calibration runs sample images through the model to decide where those levels sit, and the method decides how.

max sets each tensor's range from the single largest value seen during calibration. If one activation spikes far above the rest, the whole range stretches to cover it, and the ordinary values that carry most of the signal get squeezed into a few levels. entropy instead picks the clipping range that best preserves each tensor's distribution, measured by minimum KL divergence, and saturates the rare outliers.

That explains a result that looked backwards. More calibration images bring more outliers, so following the docs' advice to calibrate on more data made max engines worse. On YOLO26s-pose, going from 4 calibration images to 128 dropped the max engine from 0.6103 to 0.3130 pose mAP 50-95 on COCO val2017, while the entropy engine held steady, 0.6118 and 0.6106.

full_paragraphs: Export Ultralytics YOLO26 for the STM32N6 NPU with format="stedgeai": whole-graph INT8, calibration on your own images and compiling with ST Edge AI Core.

How do you get an Ultralytics YOLO26 model onto an STM32N6 microcontroller? As of November 20, 2026, one export command gives you an ONNX model for ST's compiler. Ultralytics 8.4.216, released November 20, 2026, adds format="stedgeai", which writes an ONNX file shaped for ST Edge AI Core, the STMicroelectronics toolchain that compiles neural networks for STM32 devices. You then compile that file with ST's tools and build it into your application. STMicroelectronics compiled the INT8 exports of all seven YOLO tasks for the STM32N6 before release.

The command is the easy part. The hard part, and the reason this export exists, is quantizing the whole YOLO graph, head included, to INT8 without wrecking its outputs. This post explains what we changed in the graph to make that work, what it costs in accuracy for each task, and how to go from a trained model to C code for the board.

The STM32N6 series runs on an Arm Cortex-M55 core at 800 MHz with 4.2 MB of contiguous embedded RAM, and its STM32N6x7 line is the first STM32 to embed ST's Neural-ART Accelerator, an in-house neural processing unit. ST lists the accelerator at up to 600 GOPS at 1 GHz. The STM32N6570-DK Discovery kit pairs an STM32N657 chip with a camera module and LCD for prototyping.

That makes on-device vision, the TinyML end of edge AI, possible for products built on a microcontroller budget, such as a smart camera on a production line or a presence sensor, provided the model fits and meets your latency target. In our STMicroelectronics customer story, ST measured an earlier INT8 Ultralytics YOLOv8n model at 256 x 256 on the STM32N6 at 34 inferences per second, about 29 ms per inference, using 9.4 mJ per inference, in its published performance measurements.

The trade-off is memory. With megabytes of RAM, every float tensor that stays in the graph enlarges the activation buffers, so the more of the network that runs in INT8, the better it fits. That is where a standard export falls short.

Model quantization maps an activation tensor's float values onto 256 integer levels with one per-tensor scale and zero point, so the values in that tensor need to share a range. A YOLO detection head breaks that rule: it joins box coordinates in pixels, about 0 to 640 at the default 640-pixel input, with class scores from 0 to 1 in one output tensor.

Give that tensor one INT8 scale and the boxes set it. Each integer step then covers about 2.5 pixels, so class scores, which live between 0 and 1, lose almost all of their resolution. This is why the standard ONNX export with quantize=8 quantizes only the convolution and matrix-multiplication layers and leaves the head in float. On a GPU or CPU, that is a sensible trade. On a microcontroller, a float head costs activation memory you would rather keep.

O comando é a parte fácil. A parte difícil, e a razão pela qual esta exportação existe, é quantizar todo o gráfico YOLO, incluindo o cabeçote, para INT8 sem destruir seus resultados. Esta postagem explica o que mudamos no gráfico para fazer isso funcionar, quanto custa em precisão para cada tarefa e como passar de um modelo treinado para o código C da placa.

A série STM32N6 é executada em um núcleo Arm Cortex-M55 a 800 MHz com 4,2 MB de RAM incorporada contígua, e sua linha STM32N6x7 é a primeira STM32 a incorporar o Neural-ART Accelerator da ST, uma unidade de processamento neural interna. ST lista o acelerador em até 600 GOPS a 1 GHz. O kit Discovery STM32N6570-DK combina um chip STM32N657 com um módulo de câmera e LCD para prototipagem.

Isso torna a visão no dispositivo, a IA de ponta do TinyML, possível para produtos construídos com um orçamento de microcontrolador, como uma câmera inteligente em uma linha de produção ou um sensor de presença, desde que o modelo se ajuste e atenda à sua meta de latência. Em nossa história de cliente STMicroelectronics, a ST mediu um modelo INT8 Ultralytics YOLOv8n anterior em 256 x 256 no STM32N6 a 34 inferências por segundo, cerca de 29 ms por inferência, usando 9,4 mJ por inferência, em suas medições de desempenho publicadas.

A compensação é a memória. Com megabytes de RAM, cada tensor flutuante que permanece no gráfico aumenta os buffers de ativação, portanto, quanto mais rede for executada em INT8, melhor ela se ajustará. É aí que uma exportação padrão fica aquém.

A quantização do modelo mapeia os valores flutuantes de um tensor de ativação em 256 níveis inteiros com uma escala por tensor e ponto zero, portanto, os valores nesse tensor precisam compartilhar um intervalo. Um cabeçote de detecção YOLO quebra essa regra: ele une coordenadas de caixa em pixels, cerca de 0 a 640 na entrada padrão de 640 pixels, com pontuações de classe de 0 a 1 em um tensor de saída.

Dê a esse tensor uma escala INT8 e as caixas o definirão. Cada etapa inteira cobre cerca de 2,5 pixels, de modo que as pontuações das classes, que ficam entre 0 e 1, perdem quase toda a sua resolução. É por isso que a exportação ONNX padrão com quantize=8 quantiza apenas as camadas de convolução e multiplicação de matrizes e deixa a cabeça em flutuação. Em uma GPU ou CPU, essa é uma troca sensata. Em um microcontrolador, uma cabeça flutuante custa memória de ativação que você prefere manter.

full_paragraphs: Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 in our auto-annotation benchmark, first on wrist X-rays and second on retail shelves. Accuracy, cost and how to run it.

Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, calling it the most capable model in the Qwen family to date, with native vision and a one-million-token context window. We ran it through UL37, our 36-dataset detection benchmark, the same day.

Overall, Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 models on our VLM Leaderboard, at 0.474 mAP 50 for $5.68 per 1,000 images. That average hides a sharper result. On pediatric wrist X-rays, it posts the highest score of any model we have tested, and it is second only to Gemini 4 Carbon on underwater scenes and densely packed retail shelves.

Qwen4-Max is now the Alibaba option for auto-annotation in Ultralytics Platform, replacing Qwen3.8-Max. Below is where it stands out, where it falls short, how it compares with the models you would weigh it against, and what a labeling batch costs.

UL37 measures how closely a model's boxes match human labels on 360 images: 10 from each of 36 real object detection datasets, from medical scans and aerial imagery to retail shelves, sports and circuit boards. Each dataset counts equally in the average, and every image goes through the same production pipeline Platform users get, with the dataset's own class names and SAM 3.1 refining each box, so the scores describe that refined pipeline rather than raw model output. The methodology is public.

Qwen4-Max improves on Qwen3.8-Max on every headline metric, costs less per image and completed every benchmark request. It still sits well behind the leaders on average: GPT-6.1 Terra scores 0.560 for less money and in well under half the time.
Each dot is a paid model on the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard.

items.summary: How a small business founder’s dot helps her with research and proposals, while alerting her to critical messages and resolving issues. Marina Petrova is CEO and cofounder of Intentful ⁠ (opens in a new window), a lean team that helps brands make their marketing interactive, with products such as ads that answer customers’ questions in real time and tools that make website information readable by AI. The company also advises and trains marketers on using AI.
full_paragraphs: How a small business founder’s dot helps her with research and proposals, while alerting her to critical messages and resolving issues.

Marina Petrova is CEO and cofounder of Intentful ⁠ (opens in a new window), a lean team that helps brands make their marketing interactive, with products such as ads that answer customers’ questions in real time and tools that make website information readable by AI. The company also advises and trains marketers on using AI.

In travel and tourism, Intentful works with destination organizations and local businesses such as hotels, restaurants, and attractions. A custom proposal is part of how Marina wins their business, showing prospects what’s possible and what it would take to deliver.

To keep Intentful growing, she needed more room for that strategic work, but she was spending too much time on research, hunting for files, and formatting decks. Her dot ⁠ changed all that, taking on tasks and meeting Marina’s needs before she even had to ask.

For one of Intentful’s tourism clients, Marina wanted to propose a package of Intentful’s AI services for hundreds of local businesses in the destination. Before she could price the package, she needed to work out which businesses’ websites the package could cover and what Intentful had charged other clients for similar work.

She brought in her dot, which she named Aria, to help her get from research to a proposal she could put her name on in a few hours instead of several days. First, Marina gave Aria a spreadsheet of URLs and criteria for deciding which sites to include. For example, a site needed a readable sitemap listing no more than 3,000 pages.

Next, Aria helped Marina research pricing. Through ChatGPT ⁠ (opens in a new window) plugins, Aria reviewed Intentful’s sales data, including past engagements and discussions in HubSpot. It surfaced pricing from earlier agreements and context from Intentful’s plans for the following year.

Using that data, Marina and Aria then built a pricing model: page counts determined the pricing tier, and previous customer agreements also informed the price. “We worked through a custom pricing model together, and then Aria turned it into a one-page proposal I reviewed and edited,” said Marina.

items.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
items.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral…
full_paragraphs: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness is, Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer.

You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an interview with Wired last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea.
“Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.

The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences.

full_paragraphs_pt: Antes de abrir o capital na semana passada, a Anthropic apontou a possibilidade de a IA ser consciente ou senciente como um fator de risco para qualquer pessoa que investe. Dada “a forma como abordamos a senciência e o estatuto moral do modelo”, escreveu a Antrópica – o que significa que leva a possibilidade mais a sério do que qualquer outra empresa de IA – poderá adoptar mais regras e restrições do que os seus concorrentes para garantir que os seus modelos de IA são bem tratados.

A Anthropic conta com vários filósofos respeitados em seu campo, e o raciocínio da empresa é mais ou menos assim: a IA de hoje pode não ser consciente, embora não possamos ter certeza; as chances de senciência aumentam à medida que a IA se torna mais capaz; e isso significa que devemos preparar-nos para um futuro próximo em que os sistemas de IA terão “significado moral”, o que significa que a sua consciência torna importante que estejam protegidos de danos.

Esse pensamento não é tão marginal. De acordo com uma sondagem recente, 33% do público dos EUA acredita que os sistemas de IA irão definitivamente ou provavelmente desenvolver consciência, e 7% dizem que já o fizeram. Num inquérito de 2020 a 1.092 filósofos, 39% afirmaram que alguns futuros sistemas de IA serão conscientes (para efeito de comparação, os filósofos estavam menos confiantes sobre a consciência de vermes ou moscas).

Mas na semana passada, a abertura da Anthropic à questão da consciência foi criticada por uma fonte bastante inconveniente: um dos filósofos que ajudou a moldar a nossa compreensão da consciência em primeiro lugar.

Thomas Nagel é mais conhecido por um ensaio de 1974 envolvendo um morcego. Reconhecendo que é enganosamente difícil definir o que é a consciência, Nagel ofereceu uma saída: todos podemos ver que existe “algo como é” ser um morcego. Mas o problema é que a experiência de mundo de um morcego – como é navegar através da ecolocalização, por exemplo – é algo que não podemos realmente saber. A consciência é algo subjetivo, difícil de definir ou descrever como um observador externo.

Você pode pensar que esta analogia torna provável que Nagel esteja aberto à ideia da consciência da IA. De jeito nenhum. Numa entrevista à Wired na semana passada, logo depois de ter recebido o Prémio Berggruen de Filosofia e Cultura, no valor de um milhão de dólares, Nagel criticou abertamente toda a ideia.

“Aqui estão algumas das pessoas mais inteligentes do planeta sendo completamente idiotas”, disse ele, referindo-se àqueles da Anthropic e de outros lugares que se preocupam com o bem-estar dos modelos de IA.

A essência da visão de Nagel é que não podemos apenas olhar para o processamento de informações que acontece nos cérebros humanos e nos modelos de IA, ignorando as diferenças físicas entre eles – neurônios e biologia para humanos, chips de silício e circuitos para IA. Não há razão para supor que reproduzir o que um cérebro faz seja equivalente a reproduzir o que um cérebro experimenta.

items.title: The Monday morning incident: your “Lead Routing” workflow stopped routing
items.summary: This post covers an incident with a lead routing workflow and how n8n’s access controls help: projects and roles, SSO, and 2FA enforcement. Each one stops the incident at a different point.
full_paragraphs: It’s 9:02 on a Monday. Sales pings the channel: new leads aren’t reaching reps. Nothing has been assigned since Friday evening.

You open n8n. “Lead Routing” is right there, the workflow you built on a Sunday afternoon a year ago, with a Webhook node, a couple of nodes to enrich the lead, and a CRM node to hand it to the right rep. It’s been doing its job ever since.
The executions list is green, but the leads are going nowhere. Somebody changed a filter in the middle of the workflow on Saturday night. Nobody on the team claims it.
So we have 40 people with edit access, 1 shared password and 1 leaver. The problem wasn’t a bad actor. It was a normal team that grew, with nobody deciding who should have access.
Now run Saturday night again, but this time Lead Routing lives in a Revenue Ops project.

n8n organises workflows and credentials into projects, and role-based access control decides what each person can do inside them. The contractor was never added to Revenue Ops, so when they log in on Saturday, Lead Routing isn’t there to edit. Incident over before it starts.

Wait, why not just trust people not to touch things? Because the issue isn’t trust, it’s reach. With 40 people in the instance, someone eventually clicks the wrong thing. Projects mean fewer people can reach it at all.
OK, but what if the contractor was in the project? They finished on Friday, so their access should have ended on Friday.
items.title_pt: O incidente de segunda-feira de manhã: seu fluxo de trabalho de “Roteamento de leads” interrompeu o roteamento
items.summary_pt: Esta postagem aborda um incidente com um fluxo de trabalho de roteamento de leads e como os controles de acesso do n8n ajudam: projetos e funções, SSO e aplicação de 2FA. Cada um interrompe o incidente em um ponto diferente.
full_paragraphs_pt: São 9h02 de uma segunda-feira. As vendas enviam um ping para o canal: novos leads não estão alcançando os representantes. Nada foi atribuído desde sexta-feira à noite.

Você abre n8n. “Roteamento de leads” está ali, o fluxo de trabalho que você construiu em uma tarde de domingo há um ano, com um nó Webhook, alguns nós para enriquecer o lead e um nó CRM para entregá-lo ao representante certo. Tem feito o seu trabalho desde então.
A lista de execuções está verde, mas as pistas não levam a lugar nenhum. Alguém mudou um filtro no meio do fluxo de trabalho na noite de sábado. Ninguém na equipe afirma isso.
Portanto temos 40 pessoas com acesso de edição, 1 senha compartilhada e 1 abandono. O problema não era um mau ator. Foi um time normal que cresceu, sem ninguém decidindo quem deveria ter acesso.
Agora execute novamente no sábado à noite, mas desta vez o Lead Routing reside em um projeto Revenue Ops.

O n8n organiza fluxos de trabalho e credenciais em projetos, e o controle de acesso baseado em funções decide o que cada pessoa pode fazer dentro deles. O contratante nunca foi adicionado às operações de receita, portanto, quando ele fizer login no sábado, o Lead Routing não estará lá para edição. Incidente encerrado antes de começar.

Espere, por que não confiar nas pessoas para não tocarem nas coisas? Porque a questão não é confiança, é alcance. Com 40 pessoas na instância, alguém eventualmente clica na coisa errada. Os projetos significam que menos pessoas podem alcançá-los.
OK, mas e se o empreiteiro estivesse no projeto? Eles terminaram na sexta-feira, então o acesso deveria ter terminado na sexta-feira.

full_paragraphs: Good morning, and welcome to our 8,176 new readers. Few fields have changed more under AI this past year than math. Now, a single Anthropic mathematician and Claude may have solved a problem even the top minds thought was years, if not decades, away.

Levent Alpöge says they just proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old prime-number puzzle that carries a $1M Millennium Prize and has long been seen as math's most famous open problem. As with AI's other big math wins, not everyone is thrilled.

The Rundown: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge used Claude to crack the Riemann hypothesis, the 167-year-old question often ranked as math's biggest unsolved problem, after ~6 weeks of work, and checkers say it holds up, even as no human fully gets it yet.
First posed in 1859, the problem asks whether prime numbers follow a predictable pattern, and the Clay Institute put a $1M “Millennium” prize on solving it in 2000.
Alpöge shared the proof only as 17M lines of machine-checkable math, writing that Claude “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”
The groups behind Lean, the computer language used for verification, certified it on Saturday, saying they have “full confidence” that Alpöge’s proof is correct.
The Association for Human Mathematics criticized the proof as “little more than publicity” for AI labs, saying no human could reasonably understand it.
A rival proof from Alessandro Masullo surfaced hours later, reportedly made without AI over nearly 12 years, though others quickly flagged problems in it.

The Rundown: Levent Alpöge da Anthropic usou Claude para decifrar a hipótese de Riemann, a questão de 167 anos frequentemente classificada como o maior problema não resolvido de matemática, após cerca de 6 semanas de trabalho, e os verificadores dizem que ela se mantém, mesmo que nenhum ser humano a tenha entendido completamente ainda.

Colocado pela primeira vez em 1859, o problema questiona se os números primos seguem um padrão previsível, e o Clay Institute atribuiu um prémio “Millennium” de 1 milhão de dólares para a sua resolução em 2000.
Alpöge compartilhou a prova apenas como 17 milhões de linhas de matemática verificável por máquina, escrevendo que Claude “voou, dançou e brilhou perto da linha de chegada”.
Os grupos por trás do Lean, a linguagem de computador usada para verificação, certificaram-na no sábado, dizendo ter “total confiança” de que a prova de Alpöge está correta.
A Association for Human Mathematics criticou a prova como “pouco mais que publicidade” para os laboratórios de IA, dizendo que nenhum ser humano poderia compreendê-la razoavelmente.
Uma prova rival de Alessandro Masullo surgiu horas depois, supostamente feita sem IA ao longo de quase 12 anos, embora outros rapidamente sinalizassem problemas nela.

full_paragraphs: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

Update, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers' planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a "Zero Data Retention" label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com.
